title: Endpoint routing (MapGet, MapControllers, route templates)
hook: Endpoint routing is how ASP.NET Core decides which C# method runs for a given URL and HTTP verb. MapControllers and MapGet both write into the same route table — templates, constraints, and precedence rules determine the winner.

blocks.text: Endpoint routing replaced the legacy IRouter stack in ASP.NET Core 3.0. At startup, your app registers RouteEndpoint objects — each has a route pattern (like api/orders/{id:guid}), HTTP methods, and a RequestDelegate handler. At request time, the routing middleware matches the incoming URL against all registered endpoints and selects the best match. MapControllers() registers controller actions; MapGet/MapPost register minimal API handlers. UseRouting() separates route matching from endpoint execution; UseEndpoints() (or WebApplication's implicit pipeline) runs the matched handler.

entries.plainDefinition: A pattern with literals and parameters, e.g. api/products/{id:int}.
A rule on a parameter segment — :int, :guid, :minlength(3) — to narrow matches.
entries.example: {slug:alpha:minlength(3)} matches only alphabetic slugs of 3+ chars.

entries.plainDefinition: When multiple templates match, more specific routes win over catch-alls.
entries.example: api/orders/recent beats api/orders/{id} when URL is /api/orders/recent.

entries.plainDefinition: Attributes attached to an endpoint: [Authorize], Produces, HttpMethodMetadata.
entries.example: .RequireAuthorization() on a MapGroup adds metadata to all child routes.

blocks.text: Misconfigured routing causes 404s, ambiguous match exceptions, or wrong handlers executing. Understanding route templates lets you design RESTful URLs (nouns, not verbs), apply versioning prefixes, and debug why a request hits the wrong action. In interviews, routing connects to middleware order: routing must run before authorization and endpoint execution.

blocks.title: Debug routing in Development
blocks.body: Enable logging for Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing at Debug level. The console shows which endpoint matched and why others were rejected. Use app.MapGet(...).WithName("GetOrderById") for named endpoints in link generation.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Build route table at startup
items.body: Controller discovery and MapGet calls populate EndpointDataSource with all RouteEndpoints.

items.title: Request enters routing middleware
items.body: DfaMatcher (deterministic finite automaton) finds candidate endpoints for the path.

items.title: Filter by HTTP method
items.body: GET request discards POST-only endpoints. Method mismatch yields 405 if route exists.

items.title: Select best match
items.body: More specific templates and constraints beat generic {id} catch segments.

items.title: Store endpoint in HttpContext
items.body: HttpContext.GetEndpoint() returns the match. Later middleware and the handler read metadata.

diagram.title: Route template matching
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  URL["/api/orders/3fa85f64"] --> M[DfaMatcher]
  M --> C1["api/orders/{id:guid}\n✓ constraint match"]
  M --> C2["api/orders/recent\n✗ literal mismatch"]
  M --> C3["api/{resource}/{id}\n✓ but less specific"]
  C1 --> W["Winner: OrdersController.GetById"]

snippet.label: Controller route templates and constraints
snippet.explanation: Literal segments (search, featured) must be declared to avoid being captured by {id:int}. [controller] token substitutes the class name minus 'Controller'.

snippet.label: Minimal API MapGroup with route constraints
snippet.explanation: MapGroup prefixes all routes. WithName enables CreatedAtRoute and link generation. Order of registration matters when templates overlap.

snippet.label: Link generation with named routes
snippet.explanation: Named routes decouple URL construction from hard-coded strings. CreatedAtAction/CreatedAtRoute produce Location headers per REST conventions.

blocks.title: Routing: ASP.NET Core vs Express vs NestJS
rows: Throws at startup or first request

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Overlapping routes where {id} captures literal paths like 'search' — add explicit literal routes first. Forgetting HTTP method attribute — a controller action without [HttpGet]/[HttpPost] may not map. Using catch-all {**path} too eagerly — hides routing bugs. Calling MapControllers before UseAuthorization — auth metadata won't run (middleware order topic).

blocks.text: Endpoint routing uses a DFA built at startup for O(path length) matching. EndpointDataSource is observable — hot reload in development can refresh routes. RouteEndpoint.Order and IEndpointRouteBuilder extension order affect precedence when specificity is equal. LinkGenerator resolves URLs from endpoint metadata without hitting the network. For production debugging, log HttpContext.GetEndpoint()?.DisplayName in middleware and correlate with 404 spikes in Application Insights. Custom IEndpointMatcherPolicy can implement versioning or tenant-prefix routing.

blocks.title: Routing tradeoffs
rows: Harder to see full route table at a glance
One file shows all minimal routes
Large files if not split by feature
Rare in modern Web APIs — prefer attributes

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Not knowing routing runs in middleware before the endpoint executes. Saying Express and ASP.NET routing are identical — Express has no compile-time route validation or constraint system. Unable to explain why /api/orders/search hits {id} instead of a search action — literal route specificity.

interviewTakeaways: Endpoint routing registers all routes at startup; DfaMatcher selects the best template + HTTP method per request.
Literal route segments must be declared before generic {id} parameters to avoid accidental capture.
Name endpoints (WithName) for CreatedAtRoute and link generation — avoid hard-coded URLs in production.
60s: MapControllers and MapGet write to the same table. Templates use constraints like :guid. Specificity wins. Routing middleware sets HttpContext.Endpoint before auth and handler run.
Follow-up: where does routing sit relative to UseAuthentication and UseAuthorization in the pipeline?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'first registered route wins' like Express — ASP.NET uses specificity and constraints, not just order.
Letting {id} capture reserved literals like 'search' or 'health' — add explicit routes first.
Strong answer: 'DFA matcher at startup. Literal beats parameter. Name routes for link gen. Debug with endpoint DisplayName logging.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: express.Router() with router.get('/:id') parallels MapGroup — a shared prefix and middleware. Express has no :guid constraint; you validate manually. ASP.NET rejects bad guids at routing with 404.
NestJS @Get(':id') maps like {id} but validation pipes run after routing. ASP.NET route constraints filter before the handler is invoked.
